subject.title: [Feature]:Support per-agent command lanes for multi-agent deployments

question: Should OpenClaw add a core opt-in scheduler/config surface for per-agent or per-group foreground command lanes, and what default plus aggregate-cap semantics should it use?
rationale: Source inspection proves the missing behavior, but the fix creates public config and scheduler semantics across agent, channel, hook, browser, and subagent surfaces; automation should not choose that product contract.

options.title: Design opt-in core lane policy
options.body: Keep `main` as the default, add maintainer-approved per-agent or per-group foreground lane config, and require aggregate caps plus docs and regression tests.

options.title: Defer to narrow lane surfaces
options.body: Let hook, browser, channel, and subagent lane proposals land independently without adding a top-level per-agent foreground contract yet.

options.title: Document separate gateways
options.body: Keep foreground replies on the shared `main` lane and recommend separate gateway deployments for heavy agent groups.

recommendation.title: Design opt-in core lane policy
recommendation.body: Keep `main` as the default, add maintainer-approved per-agent or per-group foreground lane config, and require aggregate caps plus docs and regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal runs through the central queue, embedded-runner, and gateway lane setup files that define this scheduler/config direction.
